_readme: This file is the single source of truth for everything the site shows. Edit it and the site updates (the dev server reloads it; a deploy rebuilds it).
AI tools: read '_aiGuide' below first — it explains every page, section and field. All content is English only.
Keys starting with '_' are documentation / planning notes only; the site ignores them. Every other key is rendered somewhere.
Empty values hide their element: '' hides a text/link/image, [] hides a list. You never need to delete a key to hide something.
Image/model paths are relative to web/public/ (e.g. 'images/acme.png' means web/public/images/acme.png). A leading '/' is fine, and full https:// URLs work too.
Arrays of objects (résumé entries, sections, work items, work details, social links) can grow or shrink: copy an existing object to add one.
IMPORTANT: resume.entries.length MUST equal model.focusPoints.length — one 3D camera stop per résumé entry, in the same order.

_fileMap.site.title: Browser tab title — injected into web/index.html at build/dev time by web/vite.config.ts
_fileMap.hero: web/src/App.tsx → Hero (heading, paragraphs, scroll cue) and the hero corner labels
_fileMap.socialLinks: web/src/ui/Resume.tsx → icon buttons inside résumé groups (picked by groups[].linkIds); icons live in web/src/ui/SocialIcons.tsx
_fileMap.works: web/src/ui/Works.tsx → the works gallery and the detail overlay's labels
_fileMap.workDetails: web/src/data/workDocs.ts → web/src/ui/Works.tsx detail overlay (matched to works items by slug)
_fileMap.model: web/src/scene/Scene.tsx → which 3D model file to load and its camera focus points
_fileMap.(loader): web/src/content.ts imports this file, defines its TypeScript types and resolves asset paths

howToUseThis: Read this block first if you are an AI tool filling in this file.
The site is a single-page, scroll-driven 3D portfolio/résumé. English only: write every value in English.
Visitors scroll top-to-bottom through these screens, in order: hero → résumé timeline → works gallery; clicking a work opens its detail overlay.
A fixed 3D character model sits behind all the text; the camera moves to a new focus point for each résumé entry as the visitor scrolls.
Each entry under 'sections' explains one top-level key of this file: what it is, where it shows up on screen, and how to write it.
Only edit data fields (keys without a leading underscore) and keep key names unchanged — the code reads them by name.
If the owner hasn't supplied a value, leave it as '' (or []) rather than inventing facts (dates, employers, numbers, links); empty values are simply hidden.

pageFlow.notes: A spinning progress ring shown until the 3D model loads. No text to fill.
Big heading + short intro paragraph over the 3D character, a 'scroll' cue at the bottom, and small labels in the corners of a thin decorative frame.
A vertical timeline on the right half of the screen. Each entry takes about one screen of scrolling, and the 3D camera focuses on a different point for each entry.
Full-height section cards that slide in horizontally as you scroll (stacked vertically on mobile). Each card has a number, a title, a tagline, a cover image and a list of works.
Full-screen article opened by clicking a work in the gallery: banner image, title, role/tags, a markdown body and an optional 'Visit site' button.

site.whereItAppears: The browser tab title (also what link previews and search engines show).

fields.title: Tab title, e.g. 'Jane Doe — Portfolio'. Keep it short.

hero.whatItIs: The first screen: who the owner is, in one glance.
hero.whereItAppears: Large centered heading + paragraph over the 3D character; a scroll cue below; corner labels in the thin frame. Everything fades out as the visitor scrolls.

fields.aboutHeading: The big heading, e.g. 'About <First name>'. 1–3 words; it's drawn in a large handwritten display font, so shorter looks better.
fields.aboutParagraphs: Intro text below the heading. Usually one paragraph of 1–3 sentences (about 40–70 words), first person. Each array item is one paragraph.
fields.scrollCueLabel: Small uppercase label above the animated scroll indicator at the bottom of the first screen, e.g. 'SCROLL'. '' hides the label.
fields.cornerMeta.name: Top-left corner: the owner's full name.
fields.cornerMeta.role: Top-left corner, below the name: job title / one-line identity, e.g. 'Full-Stack Engineer'.
fields.cornerMeta.tagline: Top-right corner: a short label, e.g. 'Portfolio — 2026'.
fields.cornerMeta.focusLine: Bottom-left corner: 2–4 keywords joined with ' · ', e.g. 'Code · Design · Play'.
fields.cornerMeta.location: Right edge (vertical text): location, e.g. 'Based in Berlin'. '' hides it.

socialLinks.whatItIs: The owner's social/profile links, shown as small monochrome icon buttons.
socialLinks.whereItAppears: Only where a résumé group lists the link's id in resume.entries[].groups[].linkIds. A link with an empty href is not shown.

fields.id: Platform id. Built-in icons: github, linkedin, x (or twitter), youtube, instagram, email, website, douyin, bilibili, xiaohongshu. Any other id shows a generic link icon.
fields.label: Platform name used as the tooltip / screen-reader label, e.g. 'GitHub'.

resume.whatItIs: The career timeline: education, jobs, ventures, side roles. Its entries are the backbone of the whole page.
resume.whereItAppears: The section heading, then a vertical timeline on the right. Each entry has a dot on the line, a period, a place/company name with optional logo, an optional role, bullet points, and optional sub-groups.
constraints: resume.entries.length MUST equal model.focusPoints.length — each entry is one 3D camera stop, matched by position. The dev console warns when they differ.
Changing the entry count means the 3D model must also be exported with that many focus nodes (see content-plan/3d-model-and-stickers-guide.md).

fields.title: Section heading above the timeline, e.g. 'Résumé' or 'Experience'. '' hides it.
fields.entries[].period: Date range, e.g. '2019 – 2022' or '2024 – Now' (en dash with spaces).
fields.entries[].place: Company, school or project name, optionally with ' · City', e.g. 'Acme Corp · London'.
fields.entries[].role: Title/degree, e.g. 'Senior Engineer' or 'B.S. in Computer Science'. '' hides it.
fields.entries[].logo.src: Optional small logo shown next to the place name, as a path relative to web/public/ (e.g. 'images/acme.png' → put the file at web/public/images/acme.png). '' shows no logo.
fields.entries[].points: 2–4 short bullet lines (under ~90 characters each): scope, achievements, clients, responsibilities. [] hides the list.
fields.entries[].groups: Optional sub-blocks inside an entry, e.g. a product, personal brand or channel. [] if not needed.
fields.entries[].groups[].heading: Sub-block title, e.g. a product or channel name.
fields.entries[].groups[].logoImg: Optional round logo/avatar before the heading, path relative to web/public/ (e.g. 'images/product.png').
fields.entries[].groups[].sub: Short descriptor after the heading, e.g. 'AI support agent'.
fields.entries[].groups[].items: 1–2 short lines, e.g. key metrics or a one-line description.
fields.entries[].groups[].linkIds: ids from socialLinks to show as icon buttons under this group, e.g. ['github','linkedin'].
fields.entries[].groups[].link: Optional URL that makes the heading clickable.

works.whatItIs: The portfolio: work grouped into a few themed sections (e.g. Client Work, Open Source, Side Projects, Talks).
works.whereItAppears: The horizontal gallery of full-height cards after the résumé. One card per section.
constraints: Every item with a slug should have a matching workDetails entry; items without one open a generic placeholder built from uiLabels.

fields.uiLabels.title: Small gallery heading in the corner, e.g. 'Works'.
fields.uiLabels.hint: Hint shown while the gallery can still be scrolled, e.g. 'Keep scrolling'.
fields.uiLabels.awardsLabel: Label before a section's awards list, e.g. 'Awards'.
fields.uiLabels.visitLabel: Text of the external-link button in a work's detail, e.g. 'Visit site'.
fields.uiLabels.closeLabel: Screen-reader label of the detail overlay's close (✕) button, e.g. 'Back'.
fields.uiLabels.detailPlaceholder: Text shown in the detail of a work that has no workDetails entry.
fields.uiLabels.phImageLabel: Caption of the image placeholder in that placeholder detail.
fields.uiLabels.phButtonLabel: Text of the dummy button in that placeholder detail.
fields.sections[].title: Section title, 1–3 words, e.g. 'Open Source'.
fields.sections[].tagline: One short line shown with the title, e.g. a company name, a stat ('2M+ downloads') or keywords.
fields.sections[].coverImage: Cover image path relative to web/public/, e.g. 'works/covers/client.jpg'. If '' or the file is missing, a numbered gradient placeholder is shown.
fields.sections[].items: The works in this section, as a flat list.
fields.sections[].items[].name: Work title as shown in the list.
fields.sections[].items[].meta: Short right-aligned stat or type, e.g. 'Interactive', '1.2M views'. Also shown as the detail's subtitle.
fields.sections[].items[].tags: Optional small muted tags, e.g. tech or platforms. Used in the detail when workDetails has no tags.
fields.sections[].items[].link: Optional external URL; used for the detail's 'Visit site' button when workDetails has no link.
fields.sections[].items[].slug: Lowercase-hyphenated id linking to a workDetails entry, e.g. 'payments-dashboard'.
fields.sections[].groups: Optional named groups of plain work titles (no detail pages), shown under items. [] if unused.
fields.sections[].awards: Optional award names shown at the bottom of the card. [] hides the awards line.
fields.sections[].footer: Optional one-line small print at the bottom of the card, e.g. the tech stack.

workDetails.whatItIs: The long-form write-up for a single work, shown full-screen when that work is clicked.
workDetails.whereItAppears: The detail overlay: banner image on top, then title, subtitle (item meta · role), tags, the markdown body, and a 'Visit site' button if a link is set.

fields.title: Detail title ('' falls back to the item's name).
fields.banner: Banner image path relative to web/public/, e.g. '/works/<slug>/banner.jpg' (file at web/public/works/<slug>/banner.jpg). If missing, a gradient placeholder with the title is shown.
fields.tags: A few short tags shown as badges, e.g. ['Interactive', 'Award Winner'].
fields.link: External URL for the 'Visit site' button.

model.whatItIs: Settings for the 3D character behind the page. Nothing here is visible text.

fields.glbPath: The 3D model file, path relative to web/public/, e.g. 'models/me.glb'.
fields.focusPoints: Ordered names of the camera focus nodes inside the glb, e.g. ['focus-1', 'focus-2', 'focus-3']. Length MUST equal resume.entries.length.
fields.framesPerNode: Frames between focus nodes in the glb's CameraAction animation. intro3d exports use 50; only change it if your model was authored differently.

_underscoreKeys.whatItIs: Planning notes the site ignores: _assetChecklist (image files still to add), model._status / _stickerTheme / _stickerCount (3D model plans), _legal (for the NOTICE file).

workDetails.title: Agentic Suite — AI Support Agent
workDetails.body:
A scalable AI-powered support agent with real-time assist — summaries and suggested responses — built for enterprise support teams.

**What I built**

- Configurable multi-agent workflows through an admin workflow builder, so each client can customise classification, troubleshooting and escalation.
- RAG-driven self-service and AI resolution flows that answer queries in real time, before a ticket is ever created.
- Intelligent routing and agent-assist that improve first-contact resolution.
- Live agent handoff across Salesforce and Zendesk, passing full conversation context to the human agent.
- A Kafka-based event-streaming design that decouples producers and consumers, keeping the multi-agent system modular, parallel and high-throughput.

**Outcome**

Up to 60% ticket deflection and 20–30% faster resolution, delivered across 4+ enterprise implementations. I also owned client-facing delivery and mentored an intern on the team.

workDetails.title: Contextual Agent
workDetails.body:
Users often struggle to explain their issue or give the context support needs. The Contextual Agent flips that around: it engages proactively, already knowing where the user is and what they're likely stuck on.

**How it works**

- A DOM intelligence pipeline extracts signals from the page the user is on.
- An LLM-powered intent prediction engine turns those signals into context-aware suggestions.
- LangGraph keeps conversational context persistent end to end.
- Redis caching avoids repeat LLM calls for returning visits to the same page, cutting inference costs.

workDetails.title: AgentHelper
workDetails.body:
An in-product, full-stack LLM support application integrated with Salesforce, giving support agents everything they need without switching tools.

**What I built**

- A context-aware system that aggregates case comments, history, Jira updates and knowledge-base content into real-time insights.
- Case intelligence: timeline reconstruction, structured summaries and response assist.
- Multilingual Response Assist using case state, sentiment, history, language detection and translation workflows.
- RAG retrieval with OpenSearch/FAISS to surface relevant articles, similar cases and experts.
- A drag-and-drop, agent-level customisable UI, tuned per client using usage insights.
- Intelligent swarming, shipped with zero QA and UAT defects.

**Outcome**

9 enterprise clients onboarded within 11 months, 95% higher agent productivity, 40% faster case resolution and a 35% improvement in CSAT.

workDetails.title: Jira Subtask Buddy
workDetails.body:
Creating Jira subtasks took 20+ clicks. Jira Subtask Buddy brings it down to 4.

I built the full MERN tool, integrated with the Jira APIs, in a single weekend — Lovable for the UI and Cursor for the backend. It saves about 7 minutes per subtask, is now actively used within the company, and keeps getting new features based on team feedback.

workDetails.title: Jira Mention Visibility
workDetails.body: A Chrome extension that surfaces Jira mentions and tagged comments in real time, so nothing gets missed and team accountability stays high.

workDetails.title: Google Meeting Scheduler
workDetails.body: A voice-activated AI meeting scheduler connected to the real Google Calendar API. It checks availability automatically and removes the back-and-forth of manual scheduling.
